references.text: The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus asks the possessed man his name, and he answers, "Legion, for we are many". Mark gives a more detailed version of the same event.
The context of this event: the possessed man from the region of the Gerasenes who meets Jesus, and who had many demons inside him.

Jesus asks for the name of the demons – this is part of a broader practice where Jesus demonstrates his authority over evil spirits, as also seen in his sending out of the twelve with power over all demons.
Jesus' teaching about unclean spirits that can return in greater numbers – the unclean spirit that brings seven other spirits worse than itself, illustrating how many demons can inhabit one person.
The parallel in Matthew regarding the possessed people in the region of the Gadarenes, where Jesus casts out demons who recognize his identity and power.
Jesus' teaching about the unclean spirit returning with seven other spirits, showing that many demons can take up residence in a single human being.
The result of Jesus' exorcism: the man who had the legion of demons now sits at peace, demonstrating Jesus' complete victory over the demons.
An unclean spirit in the synagogue in Capernaum who recognizes Jesus and names him – a parallel to the demons' interaction with Jesus where identity and name play a role.
